name: sort
description: Sorting algorithms for boru: every well-known sort (comparison, distribution, and joke/educational), driven by composable comparators, exposed as the single `Sort` namespace. Sorts return a NEW sorted List and never mutate their input.

conventions.import: import "./sort.aql"  — no `end` needed; the library imports its own boru:* deps, callers need not
conventions.call: forward, receiver (the list) LAST: `Sort.verb comparator list` (canonical). Piping `list Sort.verb comparator end` binds the same parameters; end it with `end` (or wrap in parens) so the trailing comparator cannot collect a following literal. Receiver-first-all-forward `Sort.verb list comparator` matches no signature: `boru check` (run before every `boru X`) reports `uncalled_function` and the program does not run.
conventions.comparator: A comparator is a two-argument function value returning a negative / zero / positive Integer when the first item sorts before / equal to / after the second (the sign is all that matters — same contract as the built-in `cmp`).
conventions.passing_comparators: EVERY comparator passed as an argument carries `/v` — a bare name holding a function CALLS it (boru ADR-011). Namespace comparators: `Sort.quick Sort.by-number/v list`; your own word: `Sort.quick mycmp/v list`; the built-in: `Sort.quick cmp/v list`; into a combinator: `(Sort.reverse Sort.by-number/v)`, `(Sort.by-key keyfn/v)`. `/v` replaced the retired `/r` modifier.
conventions.no_mutation: Every algorithm returns a NEW sorted List; the input List is never modified. This is the OPPOSITE of an in-place library.
conventions.distribution_sorts: The distribution sorts (counting, pigeonhole, radix-lsd, radix-msd, bucket, bead) take NO comparator and order Integers ascending; radix and bead require non-negative Integers.
conventions.import_resolution: relative to the directory of the importing file (for `boru X` and `boru check X` alike), not the working directory
conventions.errors: failures raise coded errors caught with `do [...] error [...]`; bind the result and read e.code / e.message, or inside the handler `dot code` / `get "code"` (`get` evaluates its key, so a bare `get code` is an undefined word). Codes: bad_input (a distribution sort got a non-Integer, or radix/bead got a negative, or the value range is too large), bogo_giveup (Sort.bogo exceeded its shuffle cap).
conventions.execution: boru has one execution path: `boru X` runs a static pre-flight check, then compiles to bytecode and runs on the VM. `--compile` / `--force-compile` / `--no-compile` are retired (usage errors).

Comparator.note: A two-argument function value `[b a] -> Integer` returning negative/zero/positive. The library's comparators and combinators are all of this shape. Pass one with `/v`.

by-generic.note: Order via the native `cmp`, within one type family; a mixed pair (e.g. Integer vs String) raises `incomparable`.

natural.note: Alphanumeric order: embedded digit runs compare by numeric value, so "file2" < "file10".

reverse.note: Returns a new comparator that reverses `comp` (descending).

by-key.note: Returns a comparator that orders items by the key `keyfn` extracts, compared with the native `cmp`.

comparison_sorts._call: Sort.<algo> comparator list  ->  List (new, sorted; input unchanged). Piping: list Sort.<algo> comparator end

notes.merge: Stable; the reference implementation other sorts are checked against.
notes.sort: The recommended general-purpose default (currently stable merge sort).
notes.bitonic: Generalised to any length (not only powers of two).

notes.bogo: Shuffle-until-sorted with a deterministic LCG and a hard cap; raises bogo_giveup past the cap, so use only on tiny inputs.

distribution_sorts._call: Sort.<algo> list  ->  List (Integers, ascending; NO comparator)

notes.counting: Handles negatives via a min offset; raises bad_input on non-Integers or a value range over 1e8.
notes.radix-lsd: Base-10 least-significant-digit, stable; non-negative Integers only.
notes.radix-msd: Base-10 most-significant-digit, recursive; non-negative Integers only.
notes.bucket: Value-range buckets, insertion-sorted then gathered; negatives OK.
